construct: Thyroid peroxidase at the apical follicular-cell membrane uses hydrogen peroxide to oxidize iodide and catalyzes iodination (organification) of tyrosyl residues in thyroglobulin, a required step in thyroid-hormone synthesis; loss-of-function TPO variants impair this process.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Primary congenital hypothyroidism with goiter/eutopic thyroid and biallelic TPO loss-of-function variants identifies thyroid dyshormonogenesis; TPO directly catalyzes iodide oxidation and organification onto thyroglobulin.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: NIS mediates basolateral iodide uptake; TG encodes thyroglobulin; lysosomal proteolysis releases already synthesized hormone; TSH receptor signaling regulates synthesis but is not the TPO-catalyzed reaction.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The explicit TPO genotype removes overlap with other causes of congenital hypothyroidism or dyshormonogenesis and makes the organification reaction uniquely correct.
